cost_table.fixed_comparison: 10 and 20 bp per side replayed on the same path, reported only

sources.core_claim: Jensen, Kelly, Malamud and Pedersen (SFI 22-63, 2022 version; RFS 2026): portfolios that put ML return forecasts, risk and trading costs into one objective keep positive out-of-sample net Sharpe ratios, reaching 1.38 for Portfolio-ML for an investor whose wealth reaches $10 billion by 2020, while cost-agnostic Markowitz portfolios fall to negative net returns.
sources.project_applicability: Sets the realistic ceiling for a cost-aware book and supports one optimizer holding alpha, risk and costs (design section 8); M3 (random-feature ridge) follows this line.
sources.reflection: 2022 working-paper version (the RFS 2026 numbers may differ); price-impact costs only; a $10 billion large-cap investor, not a $1M U3000 book; the full model set needs about 75 GB, so we run a reduced version.

sources.core_claim: AQR Alternative Thinking 2023 Issue 4, Exhibit A1 (Hedge Fund Research data, May 1996 - August 2023, net of fees, 87 systematic and 337 discretionary long/short equity funds including dead funds): systematic funds' Sharpe ratio is 0 / 0.2 / 0.51 / 0.87 / 1.18 at the 10th / 25th / median / 75th / 90th percentile, with median beta 0.08.
sources.project_applicability: Calibrates the target: a book net Sharpe of 0.5-1.0 is the professional median to 75th percentile, and K1's 1.19 anchor bar sits at the systematic 90th percentile.
sources.reflection: Manager-written note; fund returns are net of fees while our book has no fees but no institutional execution either; global funds, not US-only; exact publication date not printed in the snapshot.

sources.core_claim: Chen and Velikov (JFQA 58(3), May 2023): after effective bid-ask spreads, post-publication decay and restricting to the post-2005 trading-technology era, the average published anomaly is expected to earn just 4 bp per month net; the strongest anomalies net at best about 10 bp, and several methods for combining anomalies net around 20 bp.
sources.project_applicability: Single anomalies are not worth trading alone after costs; only cost-aware combinations can clear the bar, which is why the book replaces standalone anomaly tests.
sources.reflection: Spread costs only (no impact, no short-sale fees); anomaly portfolios as published; the date is the issue month.

sources.core_claim: Frazzini, Israel and Moskowitz ('Trading Costs', SSRN 3229719, August 2018 draft): on 1.7 trillion dollars of live executions by a large institutional manager across 21 developed equity markets over 19 years, price impact is well approximated by a square-root function of trade size, and actual trading costs are an order of magnitude smaller than previous studies suggest.
sources.project_applicability: Supports the impact term Y * sigma_daily * sqrt(Q/V) with Y = 0.5 in cost model v1 (design section 7) and the small impact at a $1M book.
sources.reflection: Proprietary execution data, not replicable; algorithmic institutional execution, not market-on-open orders at the first print; month-level date.

sources.core_claim: Cohen, Malloy and Pomorski (JF 2012): classifying insiders as routine or opportunistic over 1986-2007, a portfolio of opportunistic insiders' trades yields value-weighted abnormal returns of 82 bp per month, while routine insiders' trades earn essentially zero.
sources.project_applicability: Defines the insider theme (cmp_opportunistic_buy_60d) of signal library v1.
sources.reflection: Pre-2008 evidence and post-publication decay likely; the repo's standalone insider-cluster strategy was refuted and the signal now enters only as a book input; the date is the issue month.

sources.core_claim: Didisheim, Ke, Kelly and Malamud (NBER w31689): expected out-of-sample SDF performance improves with model complexity; random-feature regressions built from about 130 stock characteristics, with very many random features, beat simpler factor models in the US cross-section.
sources.project_applicability: Basis for M3 (random Fourier features, P = 4,000, ridge penalty chosen on validation folds).
sources.reflection: Gross returns; SDF framing, not a cost-aware book; heavy compute; Afsharhajari and Li (2026) argue sparsity matters inside complexity; the snapshot does not print the issue date.

sources.core_claim: Jensen, Kelly and Pedersen (JF 2023): on a new global data set of 153 factors across 93 countries, most asset pricing factors can be replicated, cluster into 13 themes and work out of sample.
sources.project_applicability: Supports theme-level composites (M0 equal-weights themes) and the theme list of signal library v1.
sources.reflection: Gross factor returns; replication is not net profitability (see Chen-Velikov); the snapshot does not print the issue date.

sources.core_claim: Gu, Kelly and Xiu (RFS 2020): trees and neural networks are the best-performing return predictors in the US cross-section, their gains come from nonlinear predictor interactions, and all methods agree on a dominant signal set that includes variations on momentum, liquidity and volatility.
sources.project_applicability: Basis for M2 (GBDT ensemble on all features, fast signals included).
sources.reflection: Gross of costs; long-short deciles are tilted to small caps; the repo's own pure price-volume model books (T-17/T-19) failed after costs; the snapshot does not print the issue date.

sources.core_claim: Fan, Liu et al. (Financial Review 57, 2022, 585-615): on the 22-factor Ehsani-Linnainmaa set and the 187-factor Hou-Xue-Zhang set, factor momentum is concentrated in 22-27% of factors and the factor momentum strategy does not outperform a buy-and-hold portfolio of the same factors (EL sample 4.07% vs 4.26% a year).
sources.project_applicability: No recency tilt beyond the preregistered M1; timing in RF1 is volatility-state based (M0V), not factor momentum.
sources.reflection: Factor portfolios, not a risk-controlled stock book; sample ends before 2024; trailing-return weighting of themes may still help in persistent regimes (our 2024-26 cross-sectional check t 3.4) while hurting at turning points.

sources.core_claim: Neuhierl, Randl, Reschenhofer and Zechner (Timing the factor zoo, 2023-03-15 version): over 300 factors and 39 predictors, timing improves almost all factor groups; past factor returns and volatility are the best single predictors; the median timed-vs-untimed improvement is about 2% a year and a timed multifactor portfolio earns about 20% more than its untimed counterpart.
sources.project_applicability: Supports the volatility-state timing variant M0V (gross and ex-ante vol target halved when VIX > 20.60).
sources.reflection: Gross factor returns; PLS aggregation of many predictors does better than any single one; no transaction costs of timing; working-paper version.

hypothesis.statement: H1 (RF1): under amendment A1 conventions the book reaches median-offset net Sharpe >= 1.19 in window A 2024-01-08..2026-06-30 (watch_recent >= 0.87), positive net excess in 2026-07-01..09-17, leave-one-phase-out minimum >= 0.87 (watch 0.60), placebo beat >= 0.95 (watch 0.90) on net and gross Sharpe, daily and Dimson beta within +-0.15, solver failures < 2% and 2x-cost excess > 0 in window A; a stress max drawdown > 20% or stress net Sharpe < -0.5 downgrades a pass to watch_recent. H2 (timing_contribution): M0V beats M0 in window A vol-matched. H3 (ml_contribution): M0X beats M0 in window A with NW t >= 2.
hypothesis.failure_mode: Signals too weak or regime-flipping in the liquid pool (Stage 0: P1000 8-book combo stress -0.23); edge concentrated in hard-to-borrow microcaps that SE_t excludes; costs at the open eat the turnover; the risk model fails to neutralise beta (D3 interim check shows realised book beta 0.3-0.7 for Stage 0 books); B infeasible under the industry constraint with ETF-only shorts.
hypothesis.measurement: evaluate.window_metrics (excess over BIL), k1_check, k2_edges on the model-cost series and on the cash-matched series, Dimson beta, solver failure counts, 2x-cost replay, 100-seed placebo for K1/K2 passers, DSR with 77 trials; per-variant turnover, cost share, exposures, leave-one-theme-out (M0_A offset 0) and fixed stress days.
hypothesis.stop_pivot: All 12 fail research_pass: book v1 refuted, infrastructure kept, expand the signal library (no parameter tuning); if M0's anchor residual IC also has NW t < 2, add signals before a v2 contract. Any pass: open the D6 forward shadow, propose a paper sleeve to the owner after 20 clean forward sessions.

decision.reason: Preregistered 2026-10-01 by the interactive lead (Opus) after the owner's recent-fit instruction, before any Stage 2 output; inherits amendment A1 run conventions of t20261001_book_v1.
decision.next_iteration_suggestion: Run RF_M0V and RF_M0X x A/B/C (30 close paths) with the T-20261001-08 runner; RF_M0/RF_M1 reuse the T-08 close paths; evaluate RF1 gates after T-20261001-13; placebo via T-20261001-14 rules.
